rationale: Kyiv Independent (Aug 1) says the gas-station campaign is spreading from the east and south into central Ukraine (Pyriatyn hit Jul 3). Russia destroyed every station in Poltava Oblast's Opishnya hromada on Aug 9, and NV (Aug 5) lists hits in Chernihiv, Sumy, Kyiv, Odesa, Poltava and even Ternopil oblasts. Recent repeat hits are still mostly in near-front Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia and Kryvyi Rih, so Poltava now leads the far-from-front cities.

On Aug 12-13 Houthi armed boats carrying drones attacked Zuqar and Mayun islands and were repelled by Yemeni army and coast guard forces stationed there (Okaz, PTOC). On Aug 19 Yemen's information minister told AFP that the Houthis plan to seize the Bab al-Mandab coast, Mokha, the Hanish islands and Mayun, so Houthi risk was raised. Government-aligned forces still hold the island, and the label AP or Al Jazeera will use is uncertain.

Sinner withdrew with a knee injury (Aug 21). Shelton won Montreal (Aug 13, beating Nakashima in the final) but lost in Cincinnati R1. Fritz won Washington. Tiafoe reached the Cincinnati final (lost to Fils, Aug 23), and Nakashima made the Montreal final and Cincinnati SF, beating Fritz. Projected seeds are Shelton 8, Fritz 9, Tien 12, Nakashima ~18, Tiafoe ~19 and Paul ~20; the draw is about Aug 27.

Ingebrigtsen is back from Achilles surgery: he won the European 5000m on Aug 10 (13:15.29) in his first race in 324 days and is auto-qualified for the UC 5000m (Sep 11 straight final) as Olympic champion. He was only 4th in the Silesia 1500m on Aug 23, behind Strand, Koech and Hocker. Yihune holds the 12:47 world lead, and Hocker is the 2025 world champion.

AFP/Le Parisien (Jul 11): the trial is Sep 10-11 with three adults. Kherbouch 'Ganito' is the alleged co-mastermind, a recidivist with a prior 7-year sentence, and was recaptured 13 days after his March escape. Khyan M. is the co-mastermind and the third is an executant who was himself sequestered by them. Kherbouch's record makes him the likeliest to get the longest sentence.

Yan remains the class of the field (71.74 WR-U20 ratified Jul 23; unbeaten in four DL meetings through Monaco). There is no news on whether she will contest Budapest (Sep 12) before the Asian Games, and the UC's 8-6-4 reduction format adds variance. Kitaguchi is auto-qualified as Olympic champion, and Kolak won the Euro title with only 62.43.

The official competition lineup (Jul 23; jury president Maggie Gyllenhaal) has 21 films; Amelio's Nessun dolore and Out of This World are not in it. The Special Jury Prize skews to political or Eastern European auteur films (No Bears, Green Border, Dear Comrades!) and Italian titles (2019, 2021, 2025). That favours Khrzhanovsky's DAU, Ali Asgari's A Bit of Light and Moretti's It Will Happen Tonight.

Talks have been frozen since the Iran war began. The Witkoff/Kushner trip to Kyiv and Moscow, promised Jul 29, has been postponed past end-August (TASS, Aug 23), and Peskov saw no grounds for optimism (Aug 20). Earlier rounds were held in Abu Dhabi and Geneva, and the US floated Miami in February, so the United States stays the top pick with Switzerland and Turkey next.

The match is MD4, Sat Sep 12 at Old Trafford. Opening weekend: Carrick's United lost 2-0 at promoted Hull (Aug 22), while Maresca's City needed late Guehi and Gvardiol goals to beat Bournemouth 2-1 (Aug 23) after Rodri left for Barcelona. United beat City 2-0 at Old Trafford in Jan 2026, so the near coin-flip is unchanged.

Japan Times/Jiji (Aug 15): with a month to go, the Sep 13 race is effectively a one-on-one between Tamaki, seeking a third term, and LDP-backed Koja (42), and neither has a decisive lead. Both are pivoting to welfare and benefits for unaffiliated voters. It remains a toss-up with a slight edge to Koja on the conservative trend.

Norris has won two in a row (Hungary in late July; Dutch GP from pole on Aug 23). Antonelli was 2nd, extending his lead to 59 over Russell and Hamilton, and Russell won the Dutch sprint. Antonelli takes a 10+ place grid drop at Monza, not Madrid. Mercedes remain the best car, but McLaren are now on par and Ferrari were close (Hamilton P4, Leclerc P5).

Tebogo won the Lausanne 200m in a dominant 19.87 on Aug 21 (SB 19.84). Lyles won the US 100m in a world-leading 9.79 but pulled up with cramp in the US 200m final (Jul 26). Both are confirmed 'Ultimate Stars' for the Sep 13 200m (Aug 18). Tate Taylor beat Tebogo in Eugene.

Pathirage keeps winning: Commonwealth gold (89.75) and Lausanne DL on Aug 21 (88.14), ahead of Chopra (88.05) and Peters (86.69), his third win over Chopra this year. Weber won the European title with a championship record (Aug 16). Nadeem is auto-qualified but out of form.

Gold Derby (Aug 17) has Seehorn at 79.7% to Russell's 14.7%. Ladbrokes (Aug 19) prices Seehorn at 1/5 and Russell at 15/4, and Kalshi had Seehorn at 77-81%. Seehorn won the Globe and Critics Choice, while Russell won the Actor Award.

SPACECOM's Gen. Whiting (Aug 12, Huntsville) said the US needs 'credible, acknowledged' kinetic and non-kinetic space fires. Today only the ground-based CCS/Meadowlands is acknowledged, and the Golden Dome interceptor demos are slated for 2027 (Aug 8). The Sep 14 resolution date may coincide with the AFA conference, the usual venue for Space Force disclosures, so the US is raised. A null outcome in 2026 is still quite possible.

Hacks leads but Widow's Bay is close: Gold Derby (Aug 17) has 74/25, Ladbrokes (Aug 19) 3/4 vs evens, and Kalshi (Jul 17) 55/43 with the gap narrowing. Matthew Rhys is a 90% favourite for Widow's Bay in Comedy Actor, and Jean Smart is a near-lock for Hacks.

The Pitt is an overwhelming favourite to repeat: Gold Derby (Aug 17) has it at 91.6%, Ladbrokes at 1/10, prediction markets around 90%, and every Ankler pundit picks it (Aug 19). Pluribus is a distant second at 6-12%, and AKOTSK is 10/1 at Ladbrokes.

There is no new evaluation news. Mundo Deportivo (Jun 11) confirms only the two bids, with the decision at the Sep 15 UEFA ExCo in Thessaloniki. Camp Nou has a 104,600 capacity, state backing and warmer Laporta-Ceferin ties, against Madrid hosting 2027 (Munich has 2028). Wembley hosted 2024 and has the Euro 2028 final.

London's final bid (Aug 6) now has a venue agreement with London Stadium/West Ham plus government funding. Nairobi submitted (Aug 10) with Ruto's personal guarantee for Kasarani. Coe said the 2029 and 2031 hosts will be named together on Sep 15 from London, Rome, Munich and Nairobi, and India/Ahmedabad is no longer listed. London is ready-made for 2029, with Nairobi possibly getting 2031.

Pakistan already urged Tehran to restrain the Houthis over threats to Saudi shipping (The Nation, Jul 23), and signed a Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan mutual defence pact in Mecca (Aug 7). China is the guarantor of the Saudi-Iran Beijing deal and has precedent (Reuters 2024). Saudi Arabia talks to the Houthis via Omani mediators, and Japan publicly said it asked Iran to urge restraint (Aug 19). No Reuters report has appeared yet.

Cruz Azul beat Toluca 3-1 in the Campeón de Campeones (Jul 25; Paradela scored twice), so they face MLS Cup holders Inter Miami in Miami on Sep 16 and Toluca is out. Miami have home advantage and Messi (scoring again in August) but were eliminated in the Leagues Cup group stage. Liga MX sides won the last three Campeones Cups.

Yemen's crisis keeps escalating: UN envoy Grundberg (Aug 7-13) warned of the gravest risk of full-scale war since the 2022 truce, the UNSC backs a 'Yemeni-led' process, and Turk warned on Aug 17. Sudan, where the US and AU are pushing a 'Sudanese-led' dialogue in August, remains the main alternative. There is no new UNGA appeal yet.

No custody-death suspension has been reported yet. The closest precedent is the Jul 20 Daily Trust case of a Suleja (Niger State) miner who died after a joint military/NSCDC raid. The NSCDC falls under the interior ministry and runs anti-illegal-mining enforcement, so its Niger State commandant remains the likeliest target.

Republicans have been silent on Trump-family self-dealing, such as Don Jr.'s Kazakhstan tungsten venture, defence-firm stakes and UAE money in World Liberty (MS NOW, Aug 20). A request would most likely come from a lame duck: retiring Judiciary member Tillis, Cassidy after his primary loss, or Cornyn, a Judiciary member who lost his primary runoff to Paxton. Cornyn replaces McConnell in the list.

Nike's deal lapsed Jul 31, but Nike launched a new Mbappe signature Mercurial on Aug 10, which he promoted. L'Equipe reports Nike has a 6-month right to match any offer, and Sportune (Aug 22) says Adidas withdrew months ago over his demands, with Puma and Under Armour weak. Reports (Aug 9-14) of an 'unexpected' new brand with an equity stake persist (Li-Ning denied), but with no announcement the question defaults to incumbent Nike.

Van vs Pantoja 2 is official as the UFC 331 main event (Aug 6). Odds are a pick'em: Pantoja opened -120/-105 and Van now -103 to -120 across books (BFO, Aug). Van is on a 7-fight streak including a defence over Taira, while Pantoja (36) returns from the elbow dislocation. Small mass is kept on replacements.

The co-main is Tsarukyan vs Mauricio Ruffy, not Oliveira, who withdrew after teammate Nascimento's death (Aug 6). Tsarukyan is a -350 to -400 favourite against Ruffy at +280 to +315; Ruffy has 13 KOs and stopped Chandler in June. The pick is shaded toward Ruffy for KO upside and Tsarukyan's withdrawal history.

Kenya's half marathon team (named Aug 21) is Ngetich, the world XC champion with a 1:03:04 PB who is 'the fastest woman in the field' and has won 5 of 6 races this year, plus Kasait, Jerono and Loleo. Chemnung, Jepchirchir and Chepkirui are not selected. Ethiopia's team is not yet known, so a large share is left unassigned.

The draw (Aug 7) is Group A Japan/Korea/Saudi/Indonesia, B Iran/Jordan/Chinese Taipei/Qatar, and C China/Philippines/Bahrain/Kazakhstan. QFs are Sep 16, SFs Sep 18, and the bronze game Sep 20. Bronze tends to go to a strong SF loser, so the six contenders (with Jordan about 0.11) are close.

No spring-1405 national accounts are out yet; last year's spring report came on Sep 22. In spring 1404 the largest subsector fall was water and electricity (-11.8%) and agriculture (-2.7%) was the worst group, while oil grew 0.8%. The April-June 2026 US naval blockade of Iranian ports should make oil the biggest decliner, but group-level reporting (oil inside 'industries and mines') remains a risk.
